case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

## Recommendation
- **Ratings (pier, this week):** Grand Haven **1**, St. Joseph **1**, Muskegon **0**, South Haven **no pier report** (I'd expect about 1).
- **Go to Grand Haven.** It has the best pier evidence and the most recent upwelling signal, but expect slow fishing.
- **Bring glow spoons or alewife**, the only lures that took pier salmon in the recent reports.
- **If you can get on a boat, that's the better bet.** Grand Haven boats were rated good in the latest report, with fish 60-110 feet down in 100-180 feet of water.

## Why
- The newest pier reports at Grand Haven and Muskegon were slow, and Grand Haven's pier action "had slowed down significantly for salmon due to the warmer water temperatures" (Grand Haven, 2025-08-13).
- I'd expect Grand Haven to be the best of the four piers this week because its pier-side water cooled 3 F in the last three days and it had the most recent upwelling wind (conditions summary for the week before Aug 19).
- Grand Haven's Aug 6 pier report was the only recent one with salmon caught on lures, on alewife and glow spoons, rated 1 (Grand Haven, 2025-08-06).
- Boats have outfished the piers: Grand Haven boats were rated 3 on Aug 13, while the pier was rated 0 the same week (Grand Haven, 2025-08-13).

## Evidence
**Recent reports (last 4 weeks)**
- Grand Haven, Aug 13: pier rated 0 (slow). Boats rated 3, with fish 60-110 feet down in 100-180 feet of water; green or yellow meat rigs and glow spoons worked (Grand Haven, 2025-08-13).
- Muskegon, Aug 13: pier rated 0; "Pier anglers casting for salmon were unsuccessful." Boats rated 2 (Muskegon, 2025-08-13).
- St. Joseph, Aug 13: rated 0 (slow); the report says "Salmon fishing slowed down this week" but doesn't say which method. Its Aug 6 pier entry was a Chinook caught on shrimp, rated 1 (St. Joseph, 2025-08-06).
- South Haven: the last four weeks have only boat reports. The Aug 13 boat report was rated 0, with the best water around 120 feet (South Haven, 2025-08-13).
- Muskegon, Aug 6: pier rated 0 ("Pier anglers tried casting spoons for salmon but were unsuccessful") (Muskegon, 2025-08-06).

**Past seasons (similar water, about 76 F)**
- Past pier reports at similar temperatures were mostly slow: St. Joseph 2024-08-21 (rated 0, "very slow"), St. Joseph 2024-07-31 (0), Grand Haven 2022-09-07 (0), Muskegon 2022-09-07 (0, "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls").
- As general history, boats did better than piers in most of those weeks. The Aug 2024 boat reports (St. Joseph, Muskegon, Grand Haven) often rated 3 with spoons.

**Conditions now**
- The tool returned a summary for the week before Aug 19, not live data. Pier-side satellite water was 74-77 F, with a 2-3 F drop in the last three days at all four ports (Grand Haven 74 F, -3; Muskegon 75 F, -3; St. Joseph 77 F, -2; South Haven 76 F, -3).
- Upwelling wind (north to east, 8+ mph) was 44 hours in the last three days at Grand Haven and Muskegon, 29 at St. Joseph and 36 at South Haven (conditions summary for the week before Aug 19).
- Buoy surface water averaged 75-77 F that week, so the offshore water was still above the 52-58 F range that Chinook prefer (NY DEC guidance, general reference).

## Caveats
- The newest reports are from Aug 13, six days old. The ratings are my estimate from weeks of slow pier reports plus a recent cooling signal, not a confirmed pier bite.
- Conditions were not live. The tool said live data was unavailable and gave the week-before summary. Pier-side water values are satellite estimates, and the buoy values are offshore.
- South Haven has no recent pier report, and the St. Joseph Aug 13 report doesn't say the method.
- Check the piers and breakwalls before you go, since the recent reports don't include closures.
